neighbours.label: a possessive determiner (my, our, her) opening a noun phrase, strongest for the speaker's own 'My' / 'Our'
fire: The coach looked up and said, "My players gave everything tonight."
At the funeral the pastor said, "Our hearts go out to the family."
The farmer told the visitors that our land has never flooded.
He paused before adding, "My brother would have loved this place."
The chairwoman wrote that our company would open two new offices.
The singer said in an interview that her sister wrote the song.
Back at the station the officer said, "Our patrol saw nothing unusual."
The author wrote in the preface that my grandfather inspired the book.
quiet: The coach looked up and said the players gave everything tonight.
At the funeral the pastor said a prayer for the family.
The farmer told the visitors that the land has never flooded.
He paused before adding, "Any brother would have loved this place."
The chairwoman wrote that the company would open two new offices.
The singer said in an interview that a friend wrote the song.
Back at the station the officer said, "The patrol saw nothing unusual."
The author wrote in the preface that a grandfather inspired the book.

notes: Top 32 are all my/our forms. Probes also fired on ' her' (0.58) and ' your' (0.34), so the unit is wider than first person. The + pole takes ' You', ' We', ' She': this side is the possessive, that side the pronoun subject.
